bio:
Hello! I am an HCI Master’s student at Seoul National University, advised by Prof. Bongwon Suh. My current research asks: How can LLM agents remember a person’s experiences over time and use those memories in future interactions?

During my undergraduate studies at SNU, I worked with Prof. Hajin Lim on personalized AI simulations and with Prof. Juho Kim at KAIST on LLM use in real classrooms.

Across my projects, I have learned to:

  • Design evaluations beyond standard metrics. Analyzing K–12 students’ interactions with AI writing support, I examined how students with different levels of writing proficiency used AI and incorporated AI-generated sentences into their essays.

  • Build robust LLM memory systems. Developing a conversational memory architecture, I focused on retrieving episodes with temporal context and preserving source dialogue to retain details that summaries may lose.

  • Study people in real-world contexts. Designing personalized AI simulations with participants’ own faces and voices, I evaluated how 21 older adults experienced them in a real-world setting.

outside:
Alongside that work, I have been building a small world building project: one place to keep the words, images, sites, people, and traces that matter to me beyond research.

I use it to collect things that do not fit neatly into academic categories, but still shape how I think and what I want to keep learning from.

Right now it includes a small Daemari translation archive, SHANUM community work, and references I keep returning to, alongside my interest in speculative thought and speculative ways of thinking.

I also like playing tennis and drawing, especially watercolor and small doodles, and I keep a drawing journal when I travel or visit new places.
